newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen edging upwards toward 124.50.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen edging upwards toward 124.50.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to have an upward bias on Wednesday with focus on moves in currencies after release of May customs-cleared trade data.

"The market will be watching the trade data. If the yen surges against the dollar after the release of the statistics, it will be a supportive factor for JGBs," a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
JGBs may also be boosted by buying of cash bonds by investors ahead of the release of the Bank of Japan's key "tankan" corporate sentiment survey on June 25, traders said.
With help from such supportive factors, the September will try for a break above a resistance of 124.37/38 and aim for 124.50, the trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus is expected to have jumped in May, with economists forecasting, on average, a rise of 157 percent from the same period last year.
The May customs-cleared trade statistics are due at 8.50 a.m. (2350 GMT Tuesday).
Although JGBs are likely to have an upward bias on Wednesday, they may reverse direction if profit-taking sales appear, a trader for another trust bank's securities unit said.
"There is a possibility that JGBs may fall below 124.00 today, especially if profit-taking emerges. Sales to take profit triggered falls in JGBs on LIFFE overnight," the trader said.
The September ended at 124.19 on LIFFE overnight, down from Tuesday's Tokyo close of 124.30.

There will also be some focus on a regular news conference by Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita at 3 p.m. (0600 GMT). His comments, however, are unlikely to provide fresh trading incentives, traders said.
